Xi Jinping was born on June 15, 1953, in Beijing, China. The son of revolutionary veteran Xi Zhongxun, he spent part of his youth in rural Shaanxi during the Cultural Revolution. Xi later studied at Tsinghua University and gradually advanced through a series of political and administrative positions at the local, provincial, and national levels.

Xi Jinping became General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party in 2012 and President of the People's Republic of China in 2013. His leadership has been associated with stronger centralized authority, anti-corruption campaigns, economic and technological development, military modernization, and an increased emphasis on China's role as a major global power.

Under Xi Jinping, China has pursued ambitious domestic and international initiatives, including the Belt and Road Initiative, expanded investment in infrastructure and advanced technology, and a more prominent role in international diplomacy. His tenure has also been marked by tighter political and social controls, increased emphasis on Communist Party leadership, and significant debate internationally over China's domestic policies and growing global influence.
